texts.preamble: Sh. Prem Singh Tomar vs Food Safety Officer on 1 April, 2022 In The Court Of Sh. Dharmesh Sharma Principal District & Sessions Judge/ Food Safety Appellate Tribunal Patiala House Court, New Delhi Fsat No. 09/2021 Sh. Prem Singh Tomar S/o Sh. Mohan Singh Tomar M/s Prem Mawa Bhandar Gate No. 2, Mawa Society Mori Gate (Khoya Auction Mandi) Delhi110006 ...Appellant Versus Food Safety Officer Department of Food Safety Govt. of Nct of Delhi 8th Floor, Mayur Bhawan Connaught Place, New Delhi110001 ...Respondent Date of filing of appeal : 22.10.2021 Date of impugned order : 08.04.2021 Date of arguments : 30.03.2022 Date of judgment : 01.04.2022 Appearance: Nemo for appellant. Fsat No. 09/2021 Prem Singh Tomar vs. Fso Page 1 of 5 Judgment
texts.facts: 1. This is an appeal preferred by the appellant Prem Singh Tomar assailing the impugned order dated 08.04.2021, whereby he has been convicted for selling food article (Khoya) meant for human consumption in terms of Section 26(1) and 26(2)(ii) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (in short "the FSS Act, 2006") read with Section 3(1)(zx) of the FSS Act, 2006. Briefly stated, the appellant stated that on 05.03.2020 at about 09:00 AM, Smt. Shalley Chauhan, the then Food Safety Officer (in short "the FSO") along with Sh. Naubat Singh, Field Assistant, as per office order/directions and under supervision of Sh. Hukam Singh, Designated Officer (DO) of District Central visited the premises of M/s Prem Mawa Bhandar, Gate No. 2, Mawa Society, Mori Gate (Khoya Auction Site), Delhi110006 and the appellant was found conducting the business at the aforesaid premises and storing and selling food article "Khoya" meant for human consumption. During the course of such inspection, the samples were collected and divided equally into four counterparts by putting them into four clean and dry glass bottles with twenty drops of formalin in each counterpart of the sample; and one of the counterpart of the sample was sent to the Food Analyst, Govt. of NCT of Delhi on 06.03.2020. The Food Analyst vide Report No. FSS/451/2018 dated 19.03.2020 submitted the report, which is as under: "The sample is substandard because milk fat of dried matter and ReichertMeissl value are less than the prescribed minimum limits of 30.0% and 28.0 respectively and ButyroRefractometer reading at 40 Deg C exceeds the prescribed maximum limit of 43.0." 4. In a nutshell, the complaint was filed by the FSO as per Rule 3.1.1(3) of the FSS Rules, 2011 and notice was issued to the appellant and on his appearance on 15.02.2021, he was supplied with the copy of the complaint and other annexures. On 11.03.2021, the appellant submitted his written submissions in which inter alia he pleaded guilty for his act and undertook that he would not repeat the wrongful act in future. 5. Suffice to state that as the appellant pleaded guilty and conceded that he was on the wrong side of the law, vide the impugned order dated 08.04.2021, the appellant was convicted u/s 26(1) and 26(2)(ii) read with Section 3(1)(zx) of the FSS Act, 2006 for being in violation of Regulation No. 2.4.6 of the Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Regulations, 2011 making it punishable u/s 51 of the FSS Act, 2006. 6. After hearing the appellant, the Ld. AO/ADM was pleased to impose penalty of Rs.1,50,000/, which is assailed in the present appeal. At the cost of repetition, the appellant submitted a written reply in his handwriting and duly signed by him whereby he pleaded guilty.
